concepts.definition: entering a financial position to neutralize exposure and reduce cash flow variance
taking a short futures position to protect physical inventory or future production from falling prices
taking a long futures position to lock in purchase prices for future raw material needs
the spot price of the asset being hedged minus the futures price of the contract used (b = S - F)
the risk that the basis will fluctuate unpredictably before the hedge is closed out
an increase in the basis over time that improves the realized selling price for a short hedger
a decrease in the basis over time that improves the net purchase price for a long hedger
